title: Weeping and joy: the not-understanding that reaches the Essence
overview:
The chapter opens with the saying "weeping is lodged in my heart on one side, and joy on the other": the soul becomes a ready vessel for G-dliness only when both come together. Then the question: joy is born of comprehension, in *bina*, yet comprehension never catches Him; *chachma*, which is *ayin*, should have the joy, but its *bittul* is the opposite of joy.

The answer is that everything has its opposite, one power in two equal lines. The power of *bina* is the power of not understanding, and the Essence, beyond understanding, is what it is really after. So the weeping comes in three levels: over the explanation not yet understood, over the *hafla'a* of *chachma*, and over the Essence that can never fit in the mind. That felt emptiness is the vessel. The comprehension is of a *tzimtzum*, but the joy reaches the Essence: now through the weeping of exile, in the future as laughter. The tears of *tikkun chatzos* prepare the way; in our days the Rebbe goes straight to the joy, but *Chassidus* that does not make a man more observant is not *Chassidus*. And this explanation, Rabbi Markel says, is the *tevuna* of the Essence.

sections.title: Weeping on one side and joy on the other: the preparation of the soul
sections.summary: Before the soul can take in the knowledge of G-dliness it has to be made a ready vessel, and that is done only by weeping and joy together, two opposites from one contemplation. One without the other, or both only on the surface, is a sure sign that nothing went in.

sections.title: The question: joy is in bina, and comprehension does not reach Him
sections.summary: Delight is in *chachma* and joy in *bina*, born of comprehension; yet the main joy is in G-dliness itself, and comprehension never catches Him. So the joy should be in *chachma*, which is *ayin*; but *chachma* is *bittul*, the opposite of joy.

phrases.he: וביאור הדברים הנה ידוע דענג ושמחה הוא בחכמה ובינה,
הענג בחכמה ושמחה בבינה
(וזהו ההפרש בין שבת ליום טוב כידוע)
כי ההשגה בשכל מוליד השמחה
שהוא שמחת הנפש
כמו שכתוב אם הבנים שמחה

blocks.text: That is the difference between *Shabbos*, *oneg* (delight), *oneg Shabbos*, and *Yom Tov*, *v'samachta b'chagecha*; as was said before, *em habanim semeicha*.

phrases.he: וידוע שעיקר השמחה דווקא באלהו״ת הוא,
phrases.en: the main thing of the *simcha* is *davka* in the *Elokus*

phrases.he: וכמו וישמחו בך דוקא
phrases.en: they will be happy *davka* by You

blocks.text: The main joy is *davka* in G-dliness, not in the explanation: they will rejoice *davka* in You. That is strange, since *bina* stops at the explanation, the *musag* (the thing grasped), and does not reach the *etzem hadavar* (the thing itself). But it makes no difference.

blocks.title: The Steelers won
blocks.text: The joy comes from the thing itself, even when you only hear about it. You hear on the radio that the Steelers won, he ran to the 10th, then the 5th: you are far away, but what makes you happy is that the guy made the goal, not the account. So we hear only an explanation, but the joy comes from the actual G-dliness.

*Bina* understands an explanation, but its *ratzon* (will), its *Keser* (crown), is *davka* for the actual thing. So *bina* has no upper or lower limit. None of the *middos* (attributes) really has one, but in a way they do; *bina* goes up and down without limit, as a *yesh*.

Going down, *bina* enters the physical world as a *yesh*, until we have cars and computers. *Chachma*, a thing of *ayin* (nothing), will not necessarily give you a way to make actual *yesh* things; *bina* does.

blocks.title: The scientific method is iyun
blocks.text: People think science is a philosophy; it is a methodology, and the methodology is *iyun* (close analysis). You make a theory, a *sevara* (a line of reasoning), and test it, as in the Talmud: maybe it is like this; how would it apply to that case? It seems to work, then someone brings a case that blows it up. An experiment tests the theory against the facts. The scientific method is *iyun*.

The scientific theory is one of the expressions of the eighth king of *Tohu* (the world of Chaos): a *bina* of *Tohu*, unconnected to G-d. Yet the eighth king does not die. In the 19th century the scientists were "very full of themselves", sure they had disproved that there is a G-d; the more they get into it, the more they see that there seems to be a Controller of the universe.

sensitivity.reason: Characterises scientists as a group as having been "very full of themselves".

blocks.text: *Bina* is into the actual thing. Here we hear explanations, but we are not really trying to understand how the world came into being; that too is a *mashal* (analogy). We are trying to understand what G-d is, and what we are doing here: that is *Chassidus*.

But *v'yismechu becha* is in the *Aibershter* (the One Above, G-d) *mamash*. Our joy in learning is not from its being an intricate study, or from understanding psychology: quantum mechanics is more intricate, and "I would get bored."

blocks.text: A joy in what? Not in the intricate study, the talking and discussing. People have philosophy groups: they get together and *hak a tchainik* (Yiddish: bang a kettle, chatter on). They even have a politics group that discusses communism, though they're all Republicans, and get a big joy and *taanug* out of the intricacies of the explanations. The joy of that *bina* comes from the beauty of the explanation. That is not what is happening here.

blocks.title: An explanation is an elegant building
blocks.text: An explanation is a *binyan*, an elegant building. Some people do mathematical problems not for the solution but for love of their elegant structures, like the ancient Arabs and Greeks who came up with algebra: their joy was in the elegance, not so much *bina*. The joy of *Chassidus*, he is telling you, comes not from the elegance but from the G-dliness, the actual subject.

blocks.text: *Bina* is into the *etzem* (essence) because it can grasp it, *davka* being the *yesh*, and reaches all levels, up and down. So the intellect going down into the physical world catches it, until a car is no longer a theory: you put a combustion engine and wheels together and make one.

blocks.title: Understanding your children
blocks.text: Engineering, aerodynamics, is intellectual, yet one wants to know how the physical world actually works. One who says "I don't understand my children" wants to understand them enough to affect their behavior (not control in a bad way); so too with politics. Some care only for the *bina* itself; but the real *inyan* of *bina* is to understand the thing itself, the *etzem*.

phrases.en: according to what we said in the last chapter, that *machshava* of *bina* actually does not catch Him

phrases.en: and this is *davka* in the *koach MaH* of the *chachma* that sees

blocks.text: But by the last chapter, the thought of *bina* does not catch Him at all. He is totally separate and wondrous, not only by our measure but beyond compare with anything we can think of.

This is *davka* in the *koach MaH* of *chachma* (the power that sees what a thing is). Not only does *bina* show that details are missing: *chachma*, from the overview of the whole, sees a wondrous thing *bina* is not describing. You see that all the particulars miss something, and you have a sight of it, into its *mahus* (what it is in itself), totally *nivdal*, separate, from what the explanation describes.

Is it by *shlila*, negation? No: negation is in *bina*, while the sight of *chachma* is *mamash* seeing, positive. But it is awakened by *bina*'s negation. There is deductive logic, inductive logic and another kind. Deductive logic says this, therefore that: from *pratim* (particulars) you reach a conclusion, a comprehension not of negation but of what the conclusion is.

blocks.title: The red ball in one of twenty pockets
blocks.text: *Hasagas hashlila* (comprehension by negation) begins like this. One of 20 people in the room has a red ball in his pocket; we check 19, and they don't. That is almost deductive logic, not a real negation: you never looked in his pocket. "It must be him, because it's not them."

blocks.title: Who controls your stomach?
blocks.text: Who controls your stomach? Not you: you're full, somebody brings a dish you love, and you can't make yourself hungry. So it must be G-d, but you have no comprehension of how. That is *hasagas hashlila*.

blocks.title: The palace in the forest
blocks.text: In general, *hasagas hashlila* is what looking around compels, as in one of the *meshalim* (analogies) for a creator. Finding a palace in the forest, food in the refrigerator, you can't wonder how many billions of years it took the stones to fall into shape. There has to be a *ba'al habayis* (an owner) to this *bira* (palace), though you don't see him.

The real *hasagas hashlila*, the *Rambam*'s (Maimonides'), is that you can't figure out what the thing is, but you can figure out what it isn't. The first is really deductive logic: the 20th guy has the ball only if you know for sure one of them has it. (The side ends here.)

You can't figure out what the *Aibershter* is, but you can figure out that He is not Jesus. He is not a person. "If you know so good, so what is it?" "The actual *mahus* you can't figure out. But I can tell you what it's not." That is the real *hasagas hashlila*: a comprehension, not in *chachma*, but an actual form of logic that figures out what the thing is not.

blocks.title: The mountain that keeps getting bigger
blocks.text: What it sees in the *mahus* is not so much what it is, just how far removed it is. You walk towards a big, big mountain and guess it is about a mile away. After three miles it looks much bigger, and maybe five miles away. The more you keep walking, the bigger and farther it gets.

blocks.title: The mountain that keeps getting bigger
blocks.text: Your sense of *hafla'a* (wondrousness) grows, then does a double take: you have no idea how big or far it is; what you see is a mirage. That is the real *hafla'a* of the *Aibershter*: realizing you are making a whole mistake, and however far you go it will keep getting bigger and farther.

sections.title: Everything has its opposite: one power in two equal lines
sections.summary: A thing's whole power comes from its opposite, as delight and pain measure each other: one power divided into two equal lines. So the push of *bina* comes from not understanding, and its real object is the Essence, which is the most not-understandable of all.

phrases.he: אך הענין הוא
phrases.en: now is the explanation

phrases.he: כידוע שבכל דבר יש היפוכו,
phrases.en: in everything there is also its opposite

phrases.he: וגם שנגלה להיפוכו ממש,
phrases.en: and even though it appears to be *mamash* its total opposite

phrases.he: אדרבה מזה עצמו נראה לעין שכל כחו אינו בא רק מכח המנגדו ממש
phrases.en: from this itself we see, from the fact that it's its total opposite, that the whole power of it comes *davka* from the opposite

blocks.text: Now the explanation: everything has its opposite in it. Though it appears to be *mamash* its total opposite, from this itself we see that its whole power comes *davka* from the opposite.
The power of understanding comes from not understanding: what pushes you to understand is *davka* that you don't understand.

Not only is the *bina* of *Chassidus* into *Elokus* (G-dliness): all *bina* is *davka* into *Elokus*, the most non-understandable thing. Other things could be understood; this cannot. So the real push of *bina* is into *Elokus*, its exact opposite.

phrases.he: ולפי ערך כח המנגד כן ימצא כח היפוכו ממש,
phrases.en: it's *davka* the power of the opposite that gives the power to the thing

phrases.he: אם כן כדבר אחד ממש הוא
phrases.en: that means that it's really *mamash* one thing

blocks.text: So the *sefarim* (the books) say of delight and pain, weeping and joy: as much as you miss somebody, that's how much you want him there and how happy you'll be when he comes. The opposite gives the thing its power: it is *mamash* one thing.

phrases.he: כמו הענג והצער,
שלפי ערך כח התענוג בדבר מה,
כן ממש לפי ערך ימצא כח התפעלות הצער,
שהוא גרעון אור הענג המנגדו
דהיינו אם יעמוד לנגדו דבר לבטל הענג ההוא להיות מן ההיפוך כו'
phrases.en: if something will prevent him from having this thing, that's how much *tza'ar* he's going to have, according to how much *oneg* he had

phrases.he: וכן להיפך,
ערך הענג מדבר מה לא יוכר רק לפי ערך הצער בהעדר אותו הדבר כו'

blocks.text: Like delight and pain: as much delight as he had in the thing, that is how much pain he will have if something prevents him from having it. And the reverse, exactly the same.

So the whole power of understanding comes from not understanding. If, as it were, we understood this better than the Mitteler Rebbe (the author), we wouldn't read this book. We read it because we don't understand it.

Someone working hard to understand something, doing *hisbonenus*, doesn't understand it. So the real power of *bina*, more than of any other *sefira*, is *Atzmus Elokus* (the Essence of G-dliness): *bina* is *mamash* rooted there, in "the totally ununderstandable thing there is", its total antithesis.

In love or fear it is not the total antithesis; in *chachma* only to an extent. In *bina* it is *mamash* the total opposite, so what *bina* really is, is *atzmuso umahuso*, His Essence and being: *mamash* non-understandable, not merely not understood yet. In *chachma* you can have a flash, an intuition into *Elokus* (not that it reaches it), so it is not the total opposite. He is telling you that the Essence is *bina*.

phrases.he: הרי כח אחד הוא ממש,
phrases.en: it's *mamash* one thing

phrases.he: רק שנחלק לב' קווין שוין ממש ושקולין
phrases.en: two equal lines going in two different directions, and they weigh exactly

phrases.he: בלתי יטה כח קו א' על ב' אפילו כקוצו של יו״ד

blocks.text: So it is *mamash* one power: the Essence, the totally non-understandable, is the actual power of *bina*, as what drives someone to understand is that he doesn't.

blocks.question: When someone knows something is unattainable, doesn't he give up hope of it?
blocks.text: Not really; it depends on the *taanug*. A heroin addict knows he can't get that first high again and keeps trying. Pain can put him into *atzvus* (melancholy) and he stops; so one should have *marirus* (bitterness), not *atzvus*: *marirus* is the opposite power that *davka* drives you.

Two equal lines going two ways weigh exactly the same. So pain and delight are the same, and not understanding and the drive to understand. That drive is strongest in *Elokus*: you can say the *mahus* of *bina* is the *mahus* of the *Aibershter*.

Look closely, and *bina* into anything, your children or psychology, comes down to wanting to understand *Elokus*. That is why the eighth king does not die: whatever he tries to understand is really *Elokus*, so he can't be disconnected. *Bina* may get hung up in details for a while, but its essence is into *Elokus*, *afilu k'kotzo shel yud*, not even by a dot.

sections.title: Joy and weeping in bina, and in the hidden delight of chachma
sections.summary: The more one has tasted G-dliness in comprehension, the more one weeps over its hiding, to the point of disgust with one's life; and above that, the hidden delight of *chachma* brings a *bittul* that throws away everything that feels itself. In each, the two lines weigh the same; and *bina*, which grasps nothing of the Essence, is the most opposite and so the most bound to it.

Offer to make him Bill Gates if he gives up *Chassidus*: no way. He can't stand this world; *Moshiach* has to come so we can study the whole time without tiring, one giant *farbrengen* (a Chassidic gathering). As by the Rebbe: study, eat and sleep at the table, and even the song between *maamarim* (discourses) is part of the *Chassidus*.

blocks.text: So too the *oneg hane'lam* (hidden delight) in *chachma*: he doesn't even know he's there anymore, *tzu tragen gor fun zich* (Yiddish: totally gone from himself). It is from the *oneg hane'lam* into the Essence, the flash of the *hafla'a*.
The opposite of it is that he will totally throw his life away against anything that will stop him from this. That means anything that will make him feel himself.

To be totally *mo'es* in his life: *mi li vashamayim v'imcha lo chafatzti va'aretz*, what do I have in heaven or want on earth, other than You? *Kala she'eri ul'vavi*, my meat and my heart are gone: nothing to do with my emotions or my meat. Only *Chassidus*.

blocks.text: Delight and weeping are *mamash* the same thing. In *chachma* too it is into the Essence, since *chachma* is the *hafla'a*, feeling he doesn't have it. But mainly it is in *bina*: *chachma* is the *ayin*, so not having it is no total negation; in *bina* it is.

In *chesed* (kindness) there is a negation too, which is why real love is into the Essence: he feels he cannot love G-d properly, though he loves Him a little. In *bina*, with all the explanations, he understands G-d not at all: a total lack.

All the *middos* come from *Elokus*, and He is *mikol ilein middos*, the opposite of all of them; but nothing like *bina*. That is why the whole thing is *bina sheb'bina* (*bina* within *bina*), the strongest power into *Elokus*.

blocks.text: So *bina* is very special, *davka* into the Essence: the lack is a *kaf shakul*, a pan of the scale weighing the same as the thing. It differs from the other *sefiros* in a couple of ways. One: only in *bina* does lacking it make you want it.
blocks.outOfPlace: After line 35 the class goes on as a free discussion of the chapter's point about bina; it is placed with the line it follows.

blocks.text: Lacking *ratzon* for something does not make you want it; lacking *taanug* in it makes you not want it. Lacking *bittul*, *chachma*, or love or hatred, does not bring them. Only *netzach* (victory) is a little like *bina*: losing, you want to win. But only in one who has *netzach*: someone not ambitious (ambition is *netzach*) is not made ambitious by lacking it. In every *midda*, once you have it, its lack makes you want more.
blocks.outOfPlace: After line 35 the class goes on as a free discussion of the chapter's point about bina; it is placed with the line it follows.

blocks.text: But in *bina* you see that even a stupid person who is not a *bina* type... You'd say it applies here too: a non-intellectual is not trying to become an intellectual; just the opposite, he thinks they're all eggheads. But it's not true. Every person, "no matter how stupid he is", wants to be a *mevin* (one who understands). Talk to the kind of people around here: they'll tell you why the Steelers lost, the quarterback made that play wrong, he should have done it like that, a whole analysis. And then they feel like they're a *mevin*.

blocks.text: Everyone's ego depends on feeling he's a *mevin*. Football is *netzach*, but they have to show they understand it: the strategy was wrong. At the back of the *shul* or at the pool hall, the stock market should have gone like this, the politics like that. Their ego depends *davka* on *bina*, because *bina* is a *yesh*.

blocks.title: The snake's new names
blocks.text:
A man told the Mitteler Rebbe he has a *hargashas hayesh*, a feeling of his own existence. Asked whether he knew what that means, he was smart enough to shut up, and the Rebbe told him a story.

After *Adam HaRishon* realized what had happened, the primordial snake cried to the *Aibershter* that nobody would listen to a snake. "Don't worry, I'll give you a new name": the *Satan*. That worked for many years, until people found him out. His next name: the *yetzer hara* (the evil inclination).
blocks.outOfPlace: After line 35 the class goes on as a free discussion of the chapter's point about bina; it is placed with the line it follows.

blocks.title: The snake's new names
blocks.text: That worked till the Baal Shem Tov, Rabbi Markel thinks (the Rebbe gave dates; he doesn't remember them). Then the new name was the *yesh*. When everybody knew about the *yesh*, around the Alter Rebbe or the Mitteler Rebbe, it became the *hargashas hayesh*. And realize, the Rebbe said: the *hargashas hayesh* is the *yesh*, the *yetzer hara*, the *Satan*, the snake.
blocks.outOfPlace: After line 35 the class goes on as a free discussion of the chapter's point about bina; it is placed with the line it follows.

blocks.text: So the *yesh* is the primordial snake, where *chachma* is *ayin* and *bina* *yesh*. Every *yesh* comes from *bina*, its left side. Upstairs the light, the *Or Ein Sof*, is the *ayin*, and the Essence the *yesh ha'amiti*, the true *yesh*. So good and bad, all the *kelipos* (husks), everything comes out of *bina*.
blocks.outOfPlace: After line 35 the class goes on as a free discussion of the chapter's point about bina; it is placed with the line it follows.

blocks.text: *Netzach* is only in one who already has it: someone not ambitious doesn't want to be. But anyone who doesn't understand wants to, and people's whole *yesh* is showing they're a *mevin* in whatever it is. And something even *netzach* lacks: *bina* is the farthest from the Essence. You understand nothing of it; all understanding is of how the *yesh* comes from the *ayin*.
blocks.outOfPlace: After line 35 the class goes on as a free discussion of the chapter's point about bina; it is placed with the line it follows.

blocks.text: *Taanug* and *ratzon* are not as much into the Essence as they should be, but a little. So too *chachma*, *bittul*, the feeling of *hafla'a*: even a regular person who understands little has some *hafla'a* toward the *Aibershter*. He is *modeh*, acknowledges: that is why he calls Him the *Aibershter*, the One higher.
blocks.outOfPlace: After line 35 the class goes on as a free discussion of the chapter's point about bina; it is placed with the line it follows.

blocks.text: So with *daas* (knowledge), connection: nobody is as connected as he should be, but there is a little. Nobody loves or fears the *Aibershter* as he should, but there is some. Nobody is great at *netzach*, overcoming bad habits to get closer to Him, but everybody overcomes a little. And *hoda'a* (acknowledgement): everybody is *modeh* to some extent... (the side ends here).

Negligible means a little is there, *batel* (nullified) in sixty or a million, but there. *Kula kamei k'la chashiv*: before the *Aibershter* it is as if it doesn't exist; not *batel* in sixty, a kind of error, but like 1 over infinity, which is not 0: the 1 is still a 1.

blocks.title: One over infinity is not zero
blocks.text: People say 1 over infinity is 0 because they don't know mathematics; there is no such real formula. 1 over 2 is a half, 1 over 3 a third, 1 over 4 a quarter: as the bottom approaches infinity the numbers get smaller, more negligible, and approach 0. But it is not actually 0, because 1 is still 1.

Vodka with a little water is still vodka, just weaker. Rabbi Markel told the student to answer: "What if I'll give you a glass of vodka and I'll spit in it?"

blocks.text: In the ocean, if I'm standing next to you, you don't care: to the ocean it's negligible, even rotten fish. But it's still there: whatever fecal matter the fishies made is totally there, the absolute amount. It is just *k'la chashiv*, considered as nothing. That is *kula kamei k'la chashiv*: there is a *kaf* there, *k'la*, *like* nothing.

Two things are *ein od milvado*: the *Aibershter*, the actual Essence; and *bina*. In *bina* there is not one iota, not even a negligible one, of understanding into the Essence: as we learned yesterday, if you understand anything, it is not the Essence. That is *davka* why *bina* takes you to the Essence: they are complete opposites.

blocks.text: Not so *chachma*, *ratzon* and the rest. *Ratzon* is wanting the Essence, so a little Essence is in it. The *hafla'a* of *chachma*, he says here, is of the Essence, not of *yesh* from *ayin*. However much *hafla'a* we, or even a big guy, have is *k'la chashiv*, nothing beside the Essence; but a little is there.

blocks.text: So with love: Avraham Avinu's "*Anochi k'afar va'efer*" is, the *Tanya* explains, a *mashal* of a burned tree that leaves only ashes. Beside the *chesed* of *Atzilus*, his *chesed* is as if nothing, but not nothing. So with the rest: in *netzach* you overcame a little, in *hod* you are *modeh* but not as you should be, in *Malchus* you accept the yoke of Heaven a little, not 100%.

blocks.text: But in *bina*, as he said: if there is any understanding there at all, it is not into the Essence. So *bina* is the exact opposite of the Essence.

blocks.question: Does this have to do with the depth above and the depth below, *omek rom* and *omek tachas*?
blocks.text: Very much. The *omek rom* is the *yesh ha'amiti*, the true *yesh*; the *omek tachas*, the *yesh hagamur*, the complete *yesh*. In the Mitteler Rebbe's *maamar* *Ata Echad*, the true *yesh* is revealed *davka* in the complete *yesh*: one who understands, and gets from it a *yeshus*, a sense of self, and joy until he is like drunk. *Bina* is wine, *yayin yesamach levav enosh*, and *bina liba*, the heart. Wine is the secrets of the Torah, *bina*; the secrets of the secrets, *bina sheb'bina*, is *Chassidus*.

blocks.text: The *hisbonenus* of *Chassidus* is called *mashke*, vodka. So the song: don't you worry, guys, we'll end up in the bar and have some vodka too (he says Las Vegas; the song has a Russian bar, the *kretchme*). Why is that *Chassidish*? Because vodka means *Chassidus*. It is sometimes called *zeks un ninetsiker*, ninety-six proof. Wrong: it's *hunderteker*, 100% alcohol.

blocks.title: The plunger: bina is the biggest vacuum
blocks.text: How can it be 100%? To unplug a sink you pump, making a vacuum that sucks it in. The biggest vacuum is *bina*. The *Aibershter* can only be in an empty place: if you're there, He won't come. But *bina* is a *yesh*, which He doesn't want! A different *yesh*: totally empty of the *Aibershter*. A 100% lack of understanding is an absolute vacuum, so it sucks Him in totally.

blocks.text: With love, a person works on himself, as in the *Chovos HaLevavos* or the like, to feel a vacuum of love or fear for the *Aibershter*, to bring Him in. But that is no 100% vacuum, nor of the Essence; and grasping any part of the *etzem* grasps all of it, so there is no vacuum. In *bina* it is the opposite: if you have any *bina*, there is no Essence there.

blocks.text: So how can it be *davka* *bina*? Back to chapter one: why *bina*, not *chachma* or the *middos*? *Ha b'ha talya*: they are *mamash* two equal lines. There the true *yesh* comes into the complete *yesh*, the *yeshus* of people: when they *shvitz* (boast), it's about how much they understand, "in whatever stupidity it is".

blocks.title: The Gra: "a convert who converted"
blocks.text: On boasting it says *b'zos yis'halel hamis'halel*; notice what it calls him. The Gra, on who becomes obligated mid-*Pesach*, lists a minor who grew up, a slave who was freed, and a *ger shenisgayer*, "a convert who converted", not "a gentile who converted", as the minor was first a minor and the slave first a slave. From this he deduces that a convert already has a convert's soul.

blocks.title: Praising himself: hallel and holelus
blocks.text: So here: why *yis'halel hamis'halel*? It says a wise man, a mighty man, a rich man, and then a *mis'halel*. *Mis'halel* does mean he praises himself, but *hallel* is also the same root as *holelus*: a wild party, a wild joy of self-abandonment. Not just meaningless joy: totally crazy joy. There could be a reason for the joy to start with, but you're not supposed to go into *holelus*.

blocks.title: Praising himself: hallel and holelus
blocks.text: Even on *Sukkos* or *Pesach* you may not get totally drunk and go into *holelus*. Here you may: he is called a *mis'halel*. He *shvitzes*, making himself a total *yesh*, and he flips out, drinking vodka, throwing up and falling down in it. *B'zos yis'halel hamis'halel*: here you can flip out with joy without bounds and tell everybody "I am the greatest": *hallelu es Hashem kol goyim*, done to himself, like Cassius Clay.

blocks.text: So *bina* is special. Chapters one to three: all the powers, above and below, are activated by *bina*, which goes up and down. Chapter 4: it is the *prat* (the particular), again *bina*. Chapter 5: no *chachma* without *bina*, nor *bina* without *chachma*, but the real thing is *bina*: you can only start to have *chachma*, but you can be *misbonen* (contemplate), and *chachma* comes from that. Now he tells us that *bina* is *nagila v'nismecha becha mamash*.

blocks.title: Opening up the aquifer
blocks.text: So the *omek tachas*, the depth below, is the underground spring on the *chachma* side that stimulates *chachma*: the *bina sheb'bina*. *Moshiach* will cut the river open into the spring's depth, so all of it comes out. The springs, the *mabu'in d'chochmasa*, are the depth below, *bina*. But the inner core of the inner core of *Abba* (*chachma*) is the inner core of *Atik* (lit. the Ancient of Days).

blocks.title: Opening up the aquifer
blocks.text: The outer spring is *chachma*; the aquifer is *Atik*, which the inner core of *Abba* goes into. But the inner core of *Ima* (lit. mother), *bina*, is that of *Abba*, the aquifer inside the aquifer: *bina* opens the spring. A regular *ish tevuna* (a man of *tevuna*, drawing an idea out) draws from the aquifer like a well; another kind opens it all, "not in pails". *Yispatchun mabu'in d'chochmasa*: *bina* did it.

blocks.title: Opening up the aquifer
blocks.text: The *mabu'in d'chochmasa* come out drop by drop, through the *chalal um'chulal*; *yispatchun* is bringing the depth out to the open. In the Flood the aquifer came out and the waters above the heavens came down: *bina* did that, as chapter 1 said. Not only reaching the aquifer inside the aquifer, but opening it onto the earth: *mal'ah ha'aretz de'ah es Hashem kamayim layam m'chasim*. That is *bina*, actually *tevuna*.

blocks.text: Up to now we learned two kinds of things. The first weeping was because he doesn't understand. The next one is from the *oneg hane'lam* in *chachma*, till he totally cannot stand anything that goes against it. And that one is of *chachma*.

In 5708 (*Tashach*) the Frierdiker Rebbe (the previous Rebbe) says what *Chassidus* calls *pnimiyus chachma*, the *koach MaH*, is its outside. The real *pnimiyus chachma* is that he cannot stand the world not studying *Chassidus*, which stands in his way: he wants *Chassidus* on the billboards of Times Square.

sections.title: The highest weeping: the Essence does not fit in the mind
sections.summary: There is a weeping above the first two: having understood the explanation, he sees that the thing itself can never fit in his mind. That total lack, felt in a way of a *yesh* of *bina*, weighs the same as the joy he would have if he grasped the Essence; it is the vessel for the secrets of the Torah, and it is the comprehension.

The lack in *bina* awakens the *hafla'a* of *chachma*, and that awakens the third level, back in understanding: he understood the explanation, to the point of total *hafla'a*, and now sees he will never understand the thing itself. It won't fit in his brain, no matter what he does.

phrases.he: אדרבה,
phrases.en: just opposite

phrases.he: כל שיעמיק יותר, יותר יפלא
phrases.en: the more you look into it, the farther it is away

phrases.he: כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: like we explained before

blocks.text: When Rabbi Akiva heard the deep secrets his eyes cried tears: his brain couldn't take them in. It is totally *bilti musag*; the more you look into it, the farther away it is. For *bina* it is more separate even than for *chachma*: "Zero. Absolute zero."

phrases.he: שמזה דוקא לבו דואג ובוכה.
שאינו בא רק מעוצם התענוג והתשוקה להשיג,
ואינו יכול כו'
וידוע שזהו עיקר בחינת הכלי לבחינת חכמה ברזין דאורייתא
phrases.en: that's *davka* the *kli* for the *chachma* in *razin d'oraysa*

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין אין מוסרין רזי תורה
אלא למי שלבו דואג בקרבו כו'
phrases.en: somebody whose heart is worrying inside of him

blocks.text: He started learning *Chassidus* to understand G-d. The weeping is the other side of that: as when his family left for the airport, the loss he feels is exactly the pleasure he had while they were there.
This is *davka* the *kli* for the *chachma* of the secrets of the Torah, a *chachma* after *bina*: not *bittul*, but actually knowing, like the Arizal or the Rebbe.

*Ein mosrin razei Torah*: how can he understand what cannot be understood? *Mosrin*: it is given to him by the *Aibershter*, who understands it, as an explanation, *l'mi shelibo do'eg b'kirbo*: to one whose heart worries that he can't understand the *Aibershter*.
All this comes only through *hisbonenus*: a beginner in *Chassidus* who says he wants to understand the *Aibershter* is lying. These are three levels, each coming from the one before.

phrases.he: אבל כשהיה משיג לעצמות אור אין סוף ממש,
phrases.en: but if he was *masig* to the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof mamash*

phrases.he: שם הוא ענין השמחה בעצמותו
phrases.en: there the *inyan* is of the *simcha* in the *Atzmus*

blocks.text: He cries totally: zero comprehension of the *Aibershter*. If he did comprehend the *atzmus Or Ein Sof mamash*, the *atzmus umahus* of the *Aibershter*, there would be the joy in the Essence. Why speak of that? Because the crying at its lack weighs the same as the joy: as much as he misses the people, that's how much he enjoys them.

phrases.he: ואף על פי שהוא גלוי העונג האלה״י הבא במורגש דווקא,
אבל שרשו באמת בעצמות התענוג הנעלם,
שממנו יצא היפוכו שהוא הבכיה מהעדרו
שהוא הפלאה והבדלה כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: it's a thing that is totally non-understandable

phrases.he: כי ב' קווין הללו שקולין גם כן בשווה ממש
phrases.en: it's exactly the same thing

phrases.he: דהיינו שלפי ערך כח עוצם וגודל התענוג שהיה מתענג בעצמות דוקא כשהיה משיגו ממש,
phrases.en: how much he would enjoy himself and be so happy if he would actually understand

phrases.he: כך ימצא כח היפוכו,
שהוא הבכיה העמוקה כשלא יכילו כלי מוחו להשיג כנזכר לעיל ודי למבין.

blocks.text: It is a joy, not a *bittul*: a felt delight, where *bittul* is a delight not felt, not even feeling he's there. At root, the weeping and the lack are the same: a thing totally non-understandable.

As in *bina* and in the *bittul* of *chachma*, the three weigh *mamash* the same: the total lack of understanding, the total weeping, and the total happiness he would have if he understood the *Aibershter* Himself.

How much he would enjoy comprehending Him is how much he cries at not comprehending, *v'hayinu hach*, as in love: somebody he doesn't enjoy he won't miss. This is activated only by the *hafla'a* of *chachma*: *bina* activates *chachma*, and *chachma* activates a higher *bina*. Now he gives the order of the levels, which is more than simply missing the *Aibershter*.

sections.title: The order of the levels, and why the not-understanding is the vessel
sections.summary: Joy from what is comprehended and weeping when it is hidden; above it the hidden delight of *chachma* and disgust with all life; above that the joy of "they will rejoice in You" and the weeping when the mind cannot hold it. The power of *bina* is the power of not understanding, like a bow drawn back: the empty glass is the vessel, and only learning makes the emptiness felt.

phrases.he: ונמצא סדר המדרגות בדבר והיפוכו כך הם,
חדוה ושמחה מגלוי אור אלה״י המושג ממש,
והיפוכו יוצא בכיה בהסתר המנגד לזה
ולמעלה מזה בבחינת ענג וחדוה הנעלם שבכח מ''ה דחכמה בעצמות אלהו״ת המהווה כו',
וכחו בהיפוכו יוצא למאוס בחייו ובחיי כל זולתו,
phrases.en: not only his own life, he can't stand the whole world

phrases.he: כמו מי לי כו'

blocks.text: So the *seder hamadreigos* (the order of the levels) in a thing and its opposite: first, joy in the explanation, and its opposite, weeping that the explanation is still hard.

Higher is the *koach MaH* of *chachma*, and its opposite: he can't stand his own life or the whole world, anybody doing anything but learning *Chassidus*. Offer him heaven: "I don't want to go to heaven."

phrases.he: ולמעלה גם מזה
phrases.en: and even higher than this

phrases.he: הענג והחדוה העצמיים בעצמות אלהו״ת דוקא,
כמו וישמחו בך ממש בגלוי כו'
phrases.en: they will actually have *simcha* in the *Atzmus mamash* in a revealed way

phrases.he: כוחו בהיפוכו יוצא כאשר לא יכילו כלי מוחו להכיל כו',
phrases.en: the opposite of *yismechu becha mamash* is when his brain cannot take it in

phrases.he: יבכה
phrases.en: then he will cry

blocks.text: Higher still is *yismechu becha mamash b'giluy*: joy in the Essence itself, revealed, in comprehension, with an explanation (this book is the explanation). Its opposite: when his brain cannot take it in, he will cry.

phrases.he: (וכמו בכיה דאוהב הנאמן בנפשו בהפרדו,
כדוד ויהונתן דאהבת נפשו אהבו,
דכתיב וישקו ויבכו כו'
phrases.en: since they were separated, they cried

phrases.he: שבא מכח ריבוי אהבה בתענוג הגדול שביחודם ודבוקם כו' וכה"ג).
phrases.en: that's how happy they were to be together

blocks.text: Like David and Yehonasan, like the airport: *vayishku vayivku*. Separated, they cried, because of how happy they were together. Exactly the same thing.
And that is *davka* the *kli* for the comprehension; more, it is the comprehension. Unlike many other things, the whole power of understanding comes from not understanding.

How much you realize you don't understand is how much power you get to do *hisbonenus*. We study because we don't understand. *Bina sheb'bina*, *pnimiyus bina* (the inner core of *bina*), is the power of not understanding, as strong as you think you don't understand; a person who thinks he understands everything asks what there is to understand by the *Aibershter*. That's why you're learning.

blocks.title: Going to college to be a doctor
blocks.text: *Bina sheb'bina* means to learn: someone in college learning to be a doctor doesn't yet know how. Learning is learning what you don't understand.

Learning *Chassidus*, he first cries that the explanation is hard. Then, as he understands, he senses how far it is: not hard but impossible, not understandable at all. That awakens the real power of *bina*: as much as he doesn't understand, that's how much he will understand.

blocks.title: The bow and the arrow
blocks.text: It goes by the negative power, like a bow: the more you pull back, the farther the arrow flies. Pulled back to absolute zero in *bina*, it goes straight into what the zero is in: the Essence.

blocks.title: That night the king could not sleep
blocks.text: The Frierdiker Rebbe's *maamar*, *Balayla hahu nadedah shnas hamelech*: the verse is said louder because the king's sleeplessness was the essence of the miracle, more than Vashti's death or Esther becoming queen. *Balayla hahu* is the exile, and *hamelech* in the Megillah is the King of the world.

blocks.title: That night the king could not sleep
blocks.text: The exile is *dormita d'Zeir Anpin*, the sleep of *Zeir Anpin* (lit. the small countenance; *dormir*, to sleep). Awake, the head is above the feet; asleep, all is on one level, and the feet think they're like the head. The *middos* are mixed up, no longer ruled by the brain. Dreams come from the liver, from *netzach*, *hod* and *yesod*: standing, the liver is the lowest of the three vessels, brain, heart and liver; asleep they are level, and the liver makes up a whole bunch of dreams. And the king woke up.

blocks.title: That night the king could not sleep
blocks.text: With *Moshiach* the King will really wake up; then He woke a little and went back to sleep. A very nice Kabbalistic explanation, but why does He sleep at all? It says *hinei lo yanum v'lo yishan shomer Yisrael*, and *ura lama sishan*, why are You sleeping? Because the exile is the dream of *Zeir Anpin*, and in a dream crazy things happen.

blocks.title: An elephant through the eye of a needle
blocks.text: You open your door and you're in China; a tree grows down from the ceiling. But towards the end of *Shaar HaYichud* (the Gate of Unity) he says you dream only what you thought in the day, its letters mixed up by the demons, never something ridiculous like an elephant through the eye of a needle. The Frierdiker Rebbe brings a quote: where could that happen? "Only in a dream." No contradiction: the Mitteler Rebbe meant a normal dream, from the day's thoughts.

blocks.title: An elephant through the eye of a needle
blocks.text: But there are nightmares, nothing like the daytime, so crazy that you realize it's a dream (in a regular dream you don't) and wake yourself up. There an elephant goes into the eye of a needle. "And that's why the *Aibershter* went to sleep."

Because He wanted a nightmare, so we should end up in Europe, and finally in America. In a nightmare the biggest thing happens: an elephant, *pila*, the biggest animal, goes into the eye of a needle, *kufa d'machta*, the littlest thing; and the roots are *pila*, *pele*, wonder, and *machta*, *chotei*, a sinner. The *Aibershter* can go into the brain not of Rabbi Akiva, but of a normal sinner, a *rasha*, "a total American *shvantz*". Where can that happen? There was a book, "Only in America". That is the reason for the exile: the thing that can't fit in his brain. In America everything is possible. They told the Frierdiker Rebbe, "This is America."

blocks.text: That is the *kli*: for comprehension of the Essence, the total lack of comprehension, felt as a *yesh* of *bina*, not even as the *ayin* of the *hafla'a* of *chachma*; and for that you must learn *Chassidus* first. Everybody says he understands nothing in G-dliness, but the lack is hidden from him: only learning shows him that he understands *mamash* zero.

The vessel of the mind cannot contain it: even an elephant through the eye of a needle has some proportion; this has none, no room at all. And this must be felt, as a *yesh*, by way of comprehension: how much it lacks understanding. That is the *kli*.

blocks.title: A glass is its emptiness
blocks.text: A *kli* is a vacuum: the main thing of a glass is its emptiness, and you can't put anything into a full one ("everybody has a full *kli*"). Proper *bina* is totally empty of G-dliness, so it is the best *kli* for it. That's why a vacuum sucks: *bina* wants to be filled with G-dliness.

That is the main matter of *bina*: to know the true nature of reality. That's what the scientist wants too; the real *mevin*, the intellectual, doesn't want to know "just some stupid thing". So that's the best *kli*.

sections.title: The answer: the joy reaches the Essence, now through weeping and in the future as laughter
sections.summary: *Bina*, most opposed to the Essence, gets closest: it gives an approximation that *chachma* fills in, and the grasp is real. So the comprehension is of a *tzimtzum* while the joy is in the Essence itself; now it comes out through the weeping of exile, and in the future, eye to eye, as laughter.

phrases.he: ובכ"ז מתורץ ענין הנזכר לעיל בשמחה שבבינה וענג שבחכמה,
דגם שההשגה עצמה היא בבחינת צמצום אור האלה״י
phrases.en: not in the actual *Elokus*, and not even in the actual *or*, but in the *tzimtzum*

phrases.he: שמשיגו,
אבל השמחה שרשה מגיע בעצמות אלהו״ת דוקא
phrases.en: but what you're *sameach* in is the *Atzmus*

blocks.text: Of all the *sefiros*, *bina* has the most opposition, so it can get the closest, and the biggest weeping is in *bina*. Its first weeping is smaller than that of *chachma*, but that wakes the third, of *bina*: even with the explanation, he sees it is not into the actual Essence.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: So the longing for the *Aibershter* is strongest *davka* in *bina*. Everywhere else you get some satisfaction; *bina*, like the Rolling Stones song, "can't get no satisfaction". Love and fear, the *hafla'a* of *chachma*, *daas*, the upper *Keser*, *ratzon* and *taanug* are all for the Essence, though you don't grasp it in them (grasping is *bina*). In *bina*, if you understand it, it is not the Essence.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: And *bina* is a perfect vacuum cleaner: the more you put in, the emptier it gets. There are ten *avodos* (services), one from each *sefira*, as there are ten general types of people; everyone is a mixture, leaning to *chesed* or *gevura*, to emotions or to brains.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: So in *avoda*: there is no *avoda* of love alone, for without *hisbonenus* there is no love. First, all the *avodos* depend on *bina*, as chapter one said; that is the whole *Kuntres HaHispaalus* (the Tract on Ecstasy): no *hisbonenus*, no *avoda*. *Malchus* is accepting the yoke of Heaven; there is love and fear; *netzach* is overcoming your bad habits by willpower; *hoda'a* is acknowledging more than you understand, and even that needs some *bina*, which is why *hod* comes out of *bina* (chapter thirty-three).
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: The other thing: all the other *avodos* give a sense of satisfaction, as with eating: the more you eat, the less hungry you get, with a certain pleasure. *Bina* is the opposite: the more you feed it, the hungrier it gets. You get joy, but the *taanug* actually gets farther away.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: And the *hafla'a* of *chachma* comes *davka* from *bina*, as these two chapters said; love and fear too come from *hisbonenus*, a *halacha* in the *Rambam*, who opens his *Yad HaChazaka* with it. Even accepting the yoke of Heaven, without intellect, needs some *bina* to start.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: As in the song from yesterday, which the Rebbe *mamash* sang himself: *tzam'a lecha nafshi kama lecha vesari*, a thirst spiritual and physical, *b'eretz tziya v'ayef bli mayim*, with no water at all: that is *davka bina*. *Kein bakodesh chazisicha*: *kein* means thus; through having no water I see You, *lir'os uzcha uchevodecha*. *Lir'os* (to see) is *chachma*; a *chizayon*, like a stargazer's, is not a clear sight: an approximation.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.question: You say *bina* is the opposite of the Essence, and that is why it can grasp it; but if you grasp it, it is not the Essence. So how does it grasp the Essence?
blocks.text: What *bina* actually is, is an approximation, or a simulation, like a *chizayon*. A *chizayon* is like the way you get a picture on a computer screen.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.title: The Rebbe's picture on the computer screen
blocks.text: His computer's background picture is the Rebbe. Magnify it and it is pixels, a bunch of dots, not really a picture of the Rebbe at all, just details. That's *bina*: it supplies details. There are levels of clarity: 320 by 400, 600 by 800, 1200 by 1500. And some pages, downloading, fill in all over, a bunch of squares, and you can't see what it is yet.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.title: The Rebbe's picture on the computer screen
blocks.text: As details fill in you see a human face, but can't tell who; it's all squares. Finally you *mamash* see the Rebbe's face, as if he stood before you. Yet it is still an approximation, just finer: from 20 by 40 to 200 by 300, to 640 by 800 on his older computer, 1200 by 1500 on newer ones. But he sees the Rebbe: "It looks to me just like when I stood in front of the Rebbe."
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.title: Your eyes are made of pixels
blocks.text: Right now you see the room. "It's not true. It's pixels. Your eyes are made of pixels." The retina is pixels of different colors working just like a TV, except they are receptors; that's why after looking at the sun you see an afterimage, until they regenerate.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.title: A movie is still pictures
blocks.text: Whatever you see is an approximation, as in a movie, where nobody moves: a bunch of still pictures, details. Yet not just an optical illusion; a little more than that, like the Rebbe's face on the screen.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.title: Close enough for folk music
blocks.text: The *chachma* fills in the spaces of the *bina*. A circle on a computer screen is a multi-gon, an octagon (eight edges) or more; a real circle has infinite edges, which 640 by 800 can't have. But close enough for folk music: your *chachma* fills in the edges and you see a circle. The *bina* and the *chachma* work together.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: Notice how he started. In chapter five he says you need all the *pratim* (particulars) of *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, *v'yevo'aru kulam b'kuntres meyuchad*. But you can't explain all the points: *min hatzorech mikol prat*, what you need from every particular, *umimeila yuvan lamevin v'yeida kama pratim acherim*. He gives the approximation, enough points, and you fill in the rest: you see a circle. That is *bina*: giving the particulars.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: Later in the book he says *chachma* comes *mimeila*, automatically: you make no effort to make it a circle, or to see the movie moving. So too, on joining to *chachma*: *bina* dissects the idea into concepts, smaller concepts, words, down to letters, and passes the letters over one at a time: the mother lends the clothing to the daughter, speech.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.title: Bah, boo: no word is ever said
blocks.text: Right now he is really talking a letter at a time: a time study would show that at no point does he say an actual word, which takes several points of time. In the book there is not a single word, only letters and spaces. But your *chachma* puts it together automatically; you don't have to think, "He said bah, then boo. Bah-boo? Oh, okay." It happens *mimeila*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: So *kein bakodesh chazisicha*: from the *chizayon* of You comes the *chachma* of *uzcha uchevodecha*, your strength and glory, already not really You but the Name, the light. And *bina* never gets the actual self? So what: it gives better and better approximations, though still not the self.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.title: The voice on the telephone
blocks.text: The picture of the Rebbe is not the Rebbe. His voice now travels as electric pulses, and what arrives is an approximation. "But it makes no difference. You're talking to me, and I'm talking to you." The grasp is actual, approximation or not: *davka bina* catches the *etzem*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: That is also why *bina* is *teshuva ila'a* (the higher return), not an emotion: it says *tashuv hanefesh el Havaya*, or *el Elokim* (he can't remember which), all the way to G-d, not part of the way. Only *bina* does that; the others are not 100%.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: *Teshuva* is also, and mainly, realizing how far you are from the *Aibershter*. That is *davka* by *bina*: only there does he see he has nothing to do with Him, that all understandings and emotions are nothing.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: The order of the levels: the weeping of *bina*, not yet understanding the explanation; of *chachma*, at the *hafla'a*, how far it is; and of *bina* again, at the totally non-understandable. The comprehension is not of G-dliness, nor of the light, but of the *tzimtzum* of the light.

phrases.he: כמו הנשמות נהנין מזיו השכינה ממש בגן עדן
גם השגתם באה על ידי צמצום כידוע
וזהו וישמחו בך דוקא,
phrases.en: actually in the *Atzmus*

phrases.he: והיינו חדווא בסטרא דא ובכיה היפוכה יוצא מכחה בג' מיני מדריגות הנזכר לעיל
וב' קווין שקולין הם
phrases.en: these are the exact two sides of the same thing

phrases.he: בשווה ממש
phrases.en: exactly equal

phrases.he: כנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: That is what *v'yismechu becha davka* means: actually in the Essence. These are exactly the two sides of the same thing, exactly equal.

phrases.he: וזהו בשמחה ובטוב לבב מרוב כל,
phrases.en: that you will worship the *Aibershter* *b'simcha uvtuv levav*, from having so much of everything

phrases.he: בהשגת המהוה
phrases.en: actual *hasaga*, not of the *mis'haveh* but of the *mehaveh*

blocks.text: *B'simcha uv'tuv levav merov kol*: serving with joy and gladness of heart from the abundance of everything. The comprehension starts only into what is brought into being; finally it is of the One who brings it into being.

phrases.he: וכמו לעתיד דכתיב עין בעין נראה כו'
phrases.en: you'll *mamash* see the *Aibershter* eye to eye

blocks.text: In the future, *ayin b'ayin yir'u*: you'll *mamash* see the *Aibershter* eye to eye. *V'amar bayom hahu hinei Elokeinu zeh*: right in front of us, *this* is the *Aibershter*, not *koh*, "like this". And then, when *Moshiach* comes, *nagila v'nismecha*. But right now it is precisely the opposite: *bivchi yavo'u davka*, *haloch yelech uvacho*.

This is also exile and redemption. The comprehension is of a *tzimtzum* of G-dly light, but the joy is in the Essence, and finally the comprehension too: a *mashal* on a *mashal*, *ulehavin davar mitoch davar*, from the externality of the One who brings into being to Him, climbing the levels in *bina*.
Our joy in *bina* is not from psychological concepts, how the human mind works, which do not interest us at all. Even in these contracted comprehensions, the joy is in G-d Himself, the *bo*.

The joy is that the *chizayon* of G-dliness slowly fills in, detail after detail, until a picture appears. The joy is from the G-dliness in a detail, the *nimshal* (what the analogy stands for), not the *mashal*: the sun is a fantastic explosion? "So who cares?"

And in the exile and the redemption: what did the *Aibershter* see to pick *davka* "idiots like us", when *bina* is from the highest things? Guys who, by the levels of how they used to be, don't have no *middos* and not much of a *sechel* (intellect) either. Why? First, with no *middos* to interfere, we can get no sense of accomplishment or enjoyment from anywhere but the *bina*. And in *bina*, the more he doesn't understand, the more he is connected to G-dliness.

Even *daas Havaya* (knowing G-d) is *davka bina*; *daas* is the result, like a mind so fired up it can't sleep.

sections.title: Tikkun chatzos: the simple tear over the sins of youth prepares the way
sections.summary: The plain tears of the midnight lament over the sins of youth repair the source of the flaw, the casting off of the yoke, and become bread for prayer; they are the first step and the preparation for the three levels of weeping, the work the *shluchim* do in the world today.

phrases.en: it's just a plain crying on his *chatos ne'urim*, on the sins of his youth

blocks.text: These two chapters, on the weeping and the joy, the tears and the *chatos ne'urim* (the sins of youth), are expanded into basically a whole book in *Derech Chaim*.

blocks.title: The plane from Los Angeles to New York
blocks.text: The simple tears over the sins of youth are *mamash* the same thing as going towards the Essence. You fly from Los Angeles to New York, 3,000 miles, and the guy on the plane says, "We've gone 1,000 miles from Los Angeles." "And how much closer to New York are we?" "Idiot, I told you, we're 1,000 miles farther from Los Angeles. So we have to be 1,000 miles closer to New York." On a line, how far you left from where you're leaving is how close you got to where you're going.

blocks.text: How far he has gone from the sins of youth is how close he has come to the *Aibershter*. So of this plain crying it says *haysa li dim'asi lechem yomam valayla*.

*Shaarei Orah* (and at length *Derech Chaim*) tells how the tear repairs the *makor hapgam*, the source of the flaw: the sins' cause, the *perikas ol* (casting off the yoke) of Heaven. And the exile of the *Shechina* comes into each G-dly spark, a spark of the *Shechina* in exile there.

Still, *bina*, *teshuva ila'a*, includes this. Especially in our days a person doesn't even understand that he casts off the yoke, as he would if he saw the master standing there. Without *hisbonenus* he doesn't know that he doesn't know, so he blesses himself that he got away.

Though they fast and think they are leaving the sins of youth (*Derech Chaim* explains this at length), **what's it going to help them?** They don't want to learn *Chassidus*; beating their chest won't help.
Real crying comes from understanding what he did. And this is the **opposite of *oneg*, which will enliven his soul**: *yagi'u ad sha'arei maves*, they will come till the gates of death.

phrases.en: this is the *hachana* to the whole *inyan* later on of the *gimmel madreigos*

blocks.text: The crying of *tikkun chatzos* is over the exile: not for the goodies of *Moshiach*, which the *Rambam* rules is not why they wanted him, but over being far from the *Aibershter*, having cast off the yoke and lost the room to study properly. This prepares the three levels to come; this crying is just a beginning, the *teshuva tata'a*.

None of this part applies nowadays: we're doing *lechatchila ariber*. But even then you have to know what you're jumping over. *Teshuva tata'a*, leaving the sins, does apply; it is done without weeping.

blocks.question: According to the Rebbe, isn't there still a weeping over the exile, only not over the sins?
blocks.text: No: the Rebbe said no more weeping over the exile, since *Moshiach* is coming, and none over the sins of youth: just leave them. That is one reason not to oppose the *shluchim* (the Rebbe's emissaries): they're preparing everybody for us.

This is the first level: these people have to put on *tefillin* and keep *Shabbos*. Leaving the sins of youth, which the weeping of *tikkun chatzos* brings about, prepares the three weepings: of *bina*, at the hard explanations; of *chachma*, at how far the *Aibershter* is; of *bina* again, at the incomprehensible.

The *shluchim* everywhere, bringing people to the first step, *teshuva tata'a*, are basically saving the external world: getting people to put on *tefillin*, keep *Shabbos*, eat kosher, learn *mishnayos*, do *ChiTaS* and all this kind of business.

blocks.title: The shliach from Singapore
blocks.text: At the *shluchim* convention in New York this weekend, someone met an old yeshiva friend, now the *shliach* of Singapore, who had brought along a *gvir* (a wealthy man) studying in a cyber yeshiva. These are the guys who supply you: a *shliach* went out first, and now there's kosher food and a synagogue for you.

That is the preparation: not like the hermetic Kabbalists, who just study *Kabbala*; you have to put on *tefillin* and eat kosher. (A listener objects that here too one can go *lechatchila ariber*.) Once you eat kosher, yes; but a man not doing *teshuva* enough to eat kosher is not really studying *Chassidus*.

sections.title: The sign of the true thing: the lower return, our days, and the tevuna of the Essence
sections.summary: Without the preparation a man fools himself: weeping alone, joy alone, or neither deep, and it does not last. A *Chassidus* that does not make a man more observant is not *Chassidus*; in our days the Rebbe says to go over the top, without weeping. And what is learned here is the *tevuna* of the Essence itself, given down to the lowest.

blocks.text: Whoever **really wants to be close to the *Aibershter*** should not fool himself and *mamash* lose his soul for nothing.

In our days it is no longer *tikkun chatzos*, but there is *teshuva*, and the sign is this: without *teshuva tata'a* there is no real *teshuva ila'a*. *Chassidus* must make you *frummer* (more observant); if it doesn't, it isn't *Chassidus*, or you didn't learn it properly. The Frierdiker Rebbe calls that *Chassidus* from the *ba'al davar*, the adversary: it looks more sophisticated.

*Tikkun chatzos*, weeping over the sins of youth, is the most external *teshuva*. Weeping lasted until the Frierdiker Rebbe, whose motto was *l'alter l'teshuva, l'alter l'geula*, immediately to *teshuva*, immediately to the redemption; in our days, the Rebbe says, it is *l'alter l'geula*.

blocks.question: Doesn't that disagree with what he says here, that there is no joy without weeping?
blocks.text: No: the weeping belonged to the exile, and we did it; now is happiness. The weeping is still there, hidden, as the joy was hidden in exile. But fixing the sins of youth is the basic level of *teshuva*; without it a person is not really studying *Chassidus*.

blocks.title: The letter from Toronto
blocks.text: He got a letter from a young *Lubavitcher bochur* (young man) in Toronto whose father is getting mixed up with Bnei Baruch, a close sister group of the Berg people, also Ashlagians. He looked through their material: they are total heretics. And the son is wondering what is happening, because his father seems to be getting more and more lax with the *mitzvos*.

sensitivity.reason: Calls a named Kabbala movement "total heretics".

blocks.text: That is the sign: someone growing lax with the *mitzvos* is not doing real *Kabbala* or *Chassidus*. *Teshuva ila'a* includes *teshuva tata'a*, and his *mitzvos* should improve automatically.

phrases.he: (ובכל זה יובן גם כן עיקר הטעם לענין הכלל הגדול בשם הרב המגיד זכרונו לברכה
במרה שחורה הטבעית,
שהוא כלי הכנה לעונג האמיתי במסירת נפש באחד כו'
ולקבלת כל רזין כו' כמו שכתוב בקונטרס באריכות ודי למבין):

blocks.text: He begins the chapter's last paragraph, on the principle in the Maggid's name, and stops at a word unclear in their copy.

He thinks it's a typo; it might be *tivi'im*, though neither he nor the student knows what that would mean (the natural scientists?). From what follows, it must be the *bechiya hativ'is*, the natural weeping: the simple crying he spoke of before.

The basic point of the end: *teshuva tata'a* is a necessary *kli*, a preparation, for learning the deeper *Chassidus*. In the Mitteler Rebbe's way you couldn't understand *Chassidus* properly without a big preparation, with crying and the like. Now it is different: the Rebbe Maharash said *lechatchila ariber*, and the Rebbe said two, the Rebbe Maharash's and his own, which is to start living like *Moshiach*.

At the end the chapter seems to back off from *bina*, the main thing, to the *avoda* of *Malchus*, from *teshuva ila'a* to *teshuva tata'a*. But this is the preparation for it: without the *mitzvos* you are doing nothing; it goes with being *frum*, and whoever isn't must start, or it won't work. *Lechatchila ariber* works now because everybody today is a *tinok shenishba* (a child taken captive), with no real sins of youth.

blocks.title: "Hey, king-o baby, let's dance"
blocks.text: A rebel against the kingdom can't do *teshuva ila'a* too: "Hey, king-o baby, let's dance together." The king hangs a rebel; he doesn't dance with him. But now they are not rebels.

The Rebbe gave various reasons. One: the weeping, the whole exile, was already done; after the Second World War especially, the Jews had such weeping that it's time for joy. The Rebbe is not disagreeing; he adjusted it for our days.

We know from experience that you can go *lechatchila ariber*, straight to *daas Havaya*: that is the Rebbe's starting to live like *Moshiach*, when *daas Havaya* is all everybody will do. The Maggid speaks of the *malchus shamayim hativ'is* (the natural kingship of Heaven), rooted from youth; that too no longer holds. He means that one who didn't *mamash* grow up *frum* will hardly come to learn these things and be affected by them.

But not by us, the Rebbe said. The chapter began with *teshuva ila'a* and ended: none without *teshuva tata'a* first. The Rebbe Maharash's *lechatchila ariber* skips the *teshuva tata'a* for *teshuva ila'a*; the Rebbe went farther, past even that, to *pnimiyus bina*, into the actual Essence. And that's chapter 6.

It is a very fantastic chapter. Its main point: *bina*, basically the study of this book's explanations, *davka* because it does not grab onto the Essence at all (if you understand it, it is not the Essence), awakens *bina liba*: with the eye of the intellect in the heart everything is seen, and the heart sees *davka* with *bina*.

So *bina* is the perfect vacuum cleaner: the more you put in, the bigger the vacuum, as the more he understands, the more he sees there's nothing there but an explanation. That is *davka* the *kushya* (difficulty) of *bina*: he wants the thing itself.

You can see it in your own *bina*: you want the actual thing, not the explanation. The first difficulty is not yet understanding the explanation. Understanding it brings the flash of *chachma*, the *hafla'a*, how far it is from understanding. That brings the third *kli*, the second of *bina*: he understands the explanation perfectly, but cannot understand the Essence. Then? He can't understand the Essence, but the all-powerful Essence can make itself understood.

That's why it says *mosrin*: it is given to him. So with Torah: *Moshe kibel Torah miSinai umesarah liYehoshua*. Moshe's own effort made him able to receive it, but the Torah itself is beyond him; it comes from the *Aibershter*, written and oral, and of the oral Torah too it says *vayomer Hashem el Moshe*. *Moshiach* will open it up; this is that opening, into the Essence.

"If it's so simple, the explanation is right here in front of us: it was already given, here it is, and anybody can grab it." No, they can't: not without the preparation, putting on *tefillin* every day and keeping kosher. Those who don't, who eat pig: "their whole brain is made out of pig meat."

blocks.text: *Davka* because of this *bina* connects all the way up, more than other things. *Chachma* coming down from the *Ein Sof* through *Atzilus* and *Beriya* to this world is not *mamash* the same *chachma*; certainly *chesed*: Avraham's love was not the love upstairs. But here we learn the explanation of the *Aibershter* Himself, and its coming down many levels *davka* shows it is the *tevuna* of the *Ein Sof*.

That it came down so far that even we can understand it shows it is the *tevuna* of the *Ein Sof*, not a lower one of *Asiya*: *davka* the *ish tevuna* brings the water to the sheep. Other things come through *hishtalshelus*; this comes direct, enclothed in *meshalim* within *meshalim*, while the *tevuna* itself has no enclothing: it is *mamash* the *Aibershter*'s.

That is *tevuna*: enclothing it in *meshalim* until a little baby can understand. In the first Temple the *Shechina* in the Ark was *Malchus* of *Atzilus* enclothed only in *Malchus* of *Beriya*, not further into *Yetzira* and *Asiya*; basically the last chapter of the *Tanya*.

This book is higher than the Holy Ark: the actual *tevuna* of the *Ein Sof*. The enclothing is the matter of *tevuna* itself: *lisvunaso ein cheker*, His *tevuna* can explain what is beyond searching, like a *tzimtzum*, and He wanted to explain it to us. So the explanation itself is the Essence.

How, if whatever you understand is not the Essence? Here you go the extra step: *pesi ya'amin l'chol davar*. The *Aibershter* wanted to explain what a *tzimtzum* is, and did: this book, *pnimiyus haTorah*, from the *Ein Sof* Himself, not *Malchus* of *Atzilus*. "It's *mamash* the *Ein Sof* is standing here and explaining it to us."

*Kudsha Brich Hu v'Oraysa v'Yisrael kula chad*: this is *mamash* the inner Torah, the *shaashua hamelech b'atzmuso*, the King's delight in Himself. David was punished for calling it *sha'ashu'im*, but he meant the outer delights. This is G-d's explanation of Himself, not of the world.

That's why we're absolutely invincible: we go not with lights, of *Atzilus* or of *Tohu*, but with the *Maor* (the source of light) itself. All over *Chassidus* it says *Chassidus* is the *Maor*; *Inyana shel Toras HaChassidus* says *Moshiach*, *Chassidus*, the *Aibershter* and the Rebbe are all one.

Chapter 6 has two main matters. One is joy and weeping in general, in all the *sefiros* and any *avoda*: basically the *Keser*, which means that as bad as you feel lacking a thing is how good you feel having it: its *taanug*.

blocks.text: And by the *taanug* is the *ratzon*: feel real bad, and you want it real bad. This returns with the *Kesarim* (the crowns): *ratzon* and *taanug* are the same, but the *ratzon* comes from the lack of the *taanug*, *davka* the weeping part; once you get what you want, you're satiated. blocks.text: So in any *midda*: Olympic athletes try so hard because they feel a lack others don't, since winning would be a great enjoyment; who cares about winning a spitting contest? Weeping and joy work this way in all the *sefiros*, not just *bina*.

blocks.text: But in *Chassidus*, *bina* is the strongest in weeping and joy: no satiation, no *taanug*. The more you understand, the more you see it is beyond understanding, and the more you want. In *bina* it is infinite, because the lack is 100%: understood, it's not the Essence. In the others, like the *hafla'a*, the insight is into the Essence itself.

blocks.text: But *bina* always has two sides, as in chapter two: *bina* and *tevuna*, from down to up, the student, and from up to down, the teacher. *Bina* goes up, to understand the actual thing: that is *hisbonenus*, learning, the student going up.

The *chachma* here is enclothed in *mashal* after *mashal*, and so is the *chesed*: really feeling even a little of the *chesed* He does us, we would go crazy, crying, laughing and rolling on the floor. blocks.text: *Tevuna* is *davka* the opposite: a tiny drop for a tiny sheep, for lowlifes like us, not the big shots; and the lower the sheep, the bigger the *tevuna*.

blocks.text: The other *sefiros* come down with a *tzimtzum*: the *chesed*, the fantastic *gevura*, the glory of *tiferes*, even the *Malchus* that reaches us through this. This is the original *tevuna*, no *tzimtzum* of it: the biggest *tevuna* is at the 3,000th *mashal*.

blocks.text: You may object that we grasp only an explanation, not the *mahus*. But the explanation itself is the *tevuna* of the *Ein Sof*: not His *bina*, how He understands, but His *tevuna*, made to explain, the Torah He came up with and gave us. Grasping it, you *mamash* grasp the Essence.

blocks.text: Grasping an explanation of a hurricane is not grasping a hurricane. Here it is different: what you grasp in any explanation is the *tevuna* of the explainer, and here that is exactly the point, literally, *lisvunaso ein cheker*.

blocks.text: Upstairs there is no such thing as *tevuna*: the *tevuna* is the Essence, all the more as this is the *tevuna* not of *Yachid* but of the *Ein Sof*. blocks.text: This is bigger than the Holy Ark, *Malchus* of *Atzilus* in *Malchus* of *Beriya*: it is *Malchus* of *tevuna* of the Essence, above *Yachid* (*lav mikol ilein middos klal*), not enclothed at all, the giver's own intellect going into the receiver.

blocks.text: That's why it is *davka bina*, for two things. From down to up it is the perfect vacuum cleaner, a total zero, not almost zero, *kula kamei k'la chashiv*, as by the others. From up to down it is its perfect opposite: the *tevuna* is *mamash ein od milvado*, "the actual Him."

blocks.text: This is also *teshuva ila'a*: *v'hanefesh tashuv ad ha'Elokim*, all the way. A very big thing about *bina*, *hisbonenus*, *Chassidus* and this book above all: it is literally the *Aibershter* Himself, bigger than the Holy Ark.
